blocks.text: The following table provides a list of error messages you might encounter when running a script for a Remediation job:

table: There was an unexpected internal error.
Workflow failed due to timeout during execution
The Remediation job reached its expiration and cannot run anymore.
Workflow expired before it could start.
The Remediation job expired before it could start the run.
The script expired during its run.
Workflow is aborted due to policy rules.
The Remediation job was aborted by an admin.
Workflow is aborted due to Remote Execution is disabled for the user/device.
The Remediation job aborted because the Remediation Settings were not enabled for the user or device.
Enable Remediation Settings for the user or device. To learn more, see Configuring Remediation Settings.
Workflow is aborted due to task error.
The Remediation job aborted because there is a task that the user's device does not recognize or support.
Edit the script to ensure all tasks are applicable to the user's device.
Workflow failed due to unsupported task category received.
The Remediation job aborted because there is a task with a category that the user's device does not recognize or support.
Edit the script to ensure all tasks with a category are applicable to the user's device. The currently supported categories are SCRIPT and LOG_COLLECTION.
Workflow failed due to policy config for this workflow is not received.
The Remediation job aborted because the script is invalid due to removal or expired certification.
Upload the Remediation job with a valid certification.
Workflow rescheduled due to user deferral.
Workflow failed due to hitting maximum defer count limit.
The Remediation job exceeded the maximum number of Remediation jobs.
The script contains an invalid task object, a null task, or the category is not supported.
Revise your script to contain valid task objects, ensure the task is not set to null, and ensure the category is supported.
Task failed due to hitting maximum retry count limit.
The Remediation job failed and reached the maximum number of retries.
Rerun the script when the user's device is available.
Task is aborted due to policy rules.
The Remediation job was aborted because an admin aborted it or there was an overriding script run.
Workflow is skipped as it's not found on device.
The Remediation job failed because an admin aborted it.
The script cannot be downloaded due to the network connection or invalid URL.
Retry downloading when the network connection is stable.
The script's certification is unverified or missing.
Check the client's device to see if there are missing certificates.
The script's certificate cannot be verified.
The script's digital signature is invalid.
Check the script's properties to validate the digital signature.
The script is not signed, or the signature is invalid.
Check the script's signature for validity as it is invalid in the Properties of Windows File Explorer.
Check if the revocation server is accessible and the OS is up-to-date. If these actions do not work, then disable the revocation check. To learn more, see Configuring Remediation Settings.
Script execution blocked by execution policy: disallowed.
The Remediation job is blocked due to Powershell Execution Policy's Restricted Mode.
Script execution blocked by execution policy: only signed scripts are allowed.
The Remediation job is blocked due to PowerShell Execution Policy's Restricted Mode.
The Remediation job has an unsupported type.
Script execution failed due to unknown result.
The script failed to run due to an unknown JSON response.
Script execution error or exception occurred.
The script failed to run due to runtime errors within the script.
Check and resolve the runtime errors in the script.
Script execution failed due to timeout.
The script failed to run due to the defined timeout.
Extend the runtime of the Remediation job. To learn more, see Viewing and Managing Jobs.
The Remediation job was aborted by an admin.
Script execution is deferred by user action.
The user postponed the Remediation job.
Script execution is declined by user action.
The user declined the Remediation job.
Script execution failed due to hitting maximum defer count limit.
The Remediation job did not run because you have exceeded the maximum number of Remediation jobs.
Wait to complete the other Remediation jobs and then re-run the job. To learn more, see Ranges & Limitations.
Script execution failed due to handler init failure.
The Remediation job failed to initialize.
Script job ID not found in ZCC SE Platform.
The Remediation job has an invalid ID in the Zscaler Client Connector Script Execution (SE) Platform.
Script execution failed due to Script Orchestrator Service is not started or unavailable.
The Remediation job cannot run because of the unavailable Script Orchestrator Service.
Log collection error or exception occurred.
Unable to collect data logs due to an internal error.
Log collection failed due to timeout.
Unable to collect data logs because the upload process exceeds runtime.
An internal error occurred during notification.
Unable to receive the user's response due to timeout.
Unable to send notification due to error initializing.
Unable to send notification because Zscaler Notification framework is disabled.
